metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Is a WR2 If Active Against Buffalo
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) practiced fully Friday after a limited Thursday session and is officially questionable against Buffalo. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Friday he expected Wilson to play. If active, Wilson belongs in lineups as a WR2. He drew 12 targets against Las Vegas in his last game and caught six for 83 yards. Geno Smith found him for 31 yards on the opening play and another 15 on the final drive. Buffalo held Justin Jefferson to three catches on 11 targets last week, but those catches went for 58 yards. Two catches of at least 19 yards accounted for most of Jefferson's production. Buffalo cornerback Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable after going from limited Thursday to a full practice Friday. RotoBaller's weekend PPR rankings put Wilson at WR17. He had two catches for 26 yards against Miami the week before the Raiders game, so his target share is a better reason to start him than the 83 yards against Las Vegas. Wilson still leads the Jets with 43 catches and 527 yards despite missing Week 9.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) listed questionable Sunday
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Wilson ended the week with a full practice. He remains on track to clear concussion protocol and be good to go for Sunday.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Officially Questionable to Play in Week 10
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) is officially questionable to play in his team's Week 10 matchup against the Buffalo Bills, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic. Wilson missed New York's Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a concussion, and he now appears to be at risk of missing a second straight contest. Across eight games in 2026, the star wideout has hauled in 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns on 63 targets. The Jets may also be without rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) against Buffalo, who is also questionable to play due to an ankle issue. In leagues where he remains available on the waiver wire, fantasy managers may want to consider stashing Jets wideout Adonai Mitchell in case Wilson and Cooper Jr. are inactive in Week 10.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) expected to play Sunday
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is "confident" that Garrett Wilson will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Glenn added that Wilson has one more step to clear before he is out of the league's concussion protocol. He has logged back-to-back limited practices this week.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Nearing clearance for Sunday
metadata.description: Wilson (concussion) has one more step to complete in concussion protocol, and Jets coach Aaron Glenn believes that will happen before Sunday's game against the Bills, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Wilson will upgrade to full participation Friday after logging limited practices earlier in the week. He's on track to return after missing just one game, but he'll still need clearance from a neurologist if Friday's practice goes as planned.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Expected to Clear Concussion Protocol to Face Bills
metadata.description: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he expects wide receiver Garrett Wilson (head) to clear the league's concussion protocol and play on Sunday against the division-rival Buffalo Bills in Week 10, according to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talks. "I see that happening," Glenn said. Wilson apparently has just one more step of the concussion protocol to clear before being given the green light to suit up on Sunday after he missed last week's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. When healthy in 2026, he has been the team's top pass-catcher, with 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns, so if he is active this weekend, Wilson should be returned to all starting fantasy lineups in a plus matchup against Buffalo's secondary. Wilson's return will be bad news for both Adonai Mitchell and rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), who have both been extremely hit or miss in the last couple of weeks as flex plays for fantasy managers. In his last game in the Week 8 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, Wilson caught six of 12 targets for 83 yards. He has double-digit targets in three games this year and already has two 100-yard performances as he works with veteran quarterback Geno Smith.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson has "One More Step" to Clear Concussion Protocol
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) has "one more step to go through" before he's cleared from concussion protocol, according to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic. Wilson missed the Jets' Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a concussion, and it appears his status for the team's Week 10 matchup against the Buffalo Bills remains unclear. Wilson has had a strong season when healthy in 2026, recording 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns on 63 targets across eight games. Even with the recent emergence of Jets rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr., Wilson remains the clear No. 1 option in his team's passing game and profiles as a solid fantasy WR2 if active in Week 10. If Wilson remains out, both Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell could see an increase in target volume against the Bills.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Wilson (concussion) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Wilson was limited in a second consecutive practice Thursday, though he took a step in the right direction, as Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports that Wilson shed the red non-contact jersey at Thursday's practice. If Wilson can practice without limitations Friday, that would go a long way in his quest to clear concussion protocol in time to face the Bills on Sunday.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) practices Thursday
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson was practicing on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson was not wearing the red jersey, a good sign for his status as he remains in concussion protocol. He continues to trend in the right direction.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Practicing again Thursday
metadata.description: Wilson (concussion) was present at Thursday's practice, Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: Wilson is taking part in practice again Thursday after being a limited participant Wednesday. An upgrade to full participation would be a step toward Wilson exiting the NFL's concussion protocol, which would put him in position to return Sunday against the Bills following a one-game absence. His participation level Thursday will be clarified later in the day.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Remains Limited on Thursday
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) was listed as a limited participant in practice on Thursday for the second straight day. A concussion caused Wilson to miss the Jets' Week 9 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on the road this past Sunday. The 26-year-old is making progress through the league's concussion protocol this week, but he might need to upgrade to full practice participation on Friday to avoid a questionable tag going into the weekend for a Week 10 contest on Sunday at home against the division-rival Buffalo Bills. Fantasy managers should be keeping a close eye on Wilson's status, as his availability will have a big effect on whether Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) will be viable flex plays against a Bills secondary that has had its issues in 2026. Wilson shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday's practice, which could be setting him up to be cleared from the concussion protocol on Friday or Saturday. If Wilson is cleared to face Buffalo this weekend, he should be in most starting fantasy football lineups as quarterback Geno Smith's No. 1 target in the passing game. Wilson has 43 catches on 63 targets for 527 yards and three touchdowns through eight games this year, but he has not found paydirt in the last three games he has played.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Participating in Individual Drills on Thursday
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), who missed the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs while remaining in the NFL's concussion protocol, was seen taking part in individual drills during Thursday's practice. Wilson was a limited practice participant on Wednesday and will likely receive the same designation with the official release of Thursday's injury report. Wilson reportedly received trade interest from both the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, but with the Jets opting to keep their roster intact, he projects to remain in a featured role upon his return. The WR20 on a points-per-game basis, Wilson profiles as a locked-in WR2 for the rest of the year.

metadata.title: Chiefs, 49ers Showed Interest in Garrett Wilson at Trade Deadline
metadata.description: While the 2-7 New York Jets opted to keep their roster intact through Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, wide receiver Garrett Wilson received trade interest from both the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers, according to Pro Football Talk. Unable to come to an agreement, both teams ended up looking elsewhere, with the Chiefs landing Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts and the 49ers adding veteran Keenan Allen. Wilson, meanwhile, remains in New York, where he has played his entire five-year career since the Jets selected him in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft. Wilson missed the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs with a concussion, but through eight weeks, he had played as the fantasy WR13 and can again be trusted as a high-end WR2 as soon as he's cleared to return to the field.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) hopeful to play in Week 10
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he's "very hopeful" Garrett Wilson will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Wilson was limited in practice on Wednesday to begin the week. He missed last week's game after getting banged up in Week 8. He'll need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Returning to limited parctice
metadata.description: Wilson (concussion) will be a a limited participant in Wednesday's practice,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athleticreports.
metadata.analysis: That's a step in the right direction for Wilson, who didn't practice last week before being ruled out for Week 9 action. Given that the wideout is still limited at this stage, Wilson has some hurdles to clear before he's cleared from the NFL's concussion protocol, however, if he's able return to action this weekend versus the Bills, he'll reclaim his lead role in a WR corps that was paced by Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell in his absence from this past Sunday's loss to the Chiefs.

metadata.title: Aaron Glenn "Very Hopeful" That Garrett Wilson Will Play in Week 10
metadata.description: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said he is "very hopeful" that wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) will play in Week 10 against the division-rival Buffalo Bills, according to Connor Hughes of SNY. The Jets should get their WR1 back for the contest against Buffalo after he sat out of Sunday's Week 9 blowout loss in Kansas City to the Chiefs. New York's offense struggled to move the ball effectively in a hostile environment without their top receiver last weekend. If the 26-year-old can clear the league's concussion protocol this week, fantasy managers should be throwing him back into their starting lineups against a Bills secondary that has had its issues this year defending the pass. Through eight games played in 2026, Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns as quarterback Geno Smith's go-to target. Wilson's return would be bad news for any fantasy managers considering using either Adonai Mitchell or rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. in their lineups in Week 10. In the Week 8 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, Cooper did not catch any passes, while Mitchell put up a donut for his fantasy managers without Wilson in the fold on Sunday in Kansas City. Both WRs will be volatile if Wilson returns from his concussion.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) ruled out Sunday
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup between the New York Jets and Kansas City Chiefs according to Rich Cimini.
metadata.analysis: Wilson will be sidelined for head coach Aaron Glenn after being unable to progress through concussion issues throughout the week, setting up Adonai Mitchell and Omari Cooper for increased targets against the Chiefs Sunday.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Ruled out for Sunday
metadata.description: Wilson (concussion) is out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: With Wilson set to miss the contest, the Jets will be without their top wide receiver as he remains in concussion protocol. His absence leaves targets available to Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, who get significant boosts to their respective Week 9 fantasy stocks, while Isaiah Williams figures to handle WR3 duties.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Ruled Out for Week 9 with Concussion
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) has officially been ruled out for his team's Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, per ESPN's Rich Cimini. Wilson has been the Jets' top pass-catcher so far this season, recording 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns on 63 targets across eight games. While the 26-year-old should have a chance to return to the field in Week 10 against the Buffalo Bills, he will be unable to suit up against Kansas City. Without him, Jets wideouts Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. should both see increased workloads and could be worth starting in deeper fantasy leagues. Both wide receivers have proven capable of big performances even while sharing the field with Wilson, as Mitchell recorded 142 yards and a touchdown in Week 8 and Cooper Jr. logged back-to-back games with 100-plus yards and a touchdown in Weeks 6 and 7.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Does not practice Thursday
metadata.description: Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson remains in concussion protocol and has not practiced thus far this week. He was placed in protocol midweek, which makes it an uphill climb for him to be cleared for Sunday's game at the Chiefs. If Wilson can't clear protocol, fantasy managers can expect more targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) not practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson was not seen practicing on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson continues to trend in the wrong direction to play this week as he remains in concussion protocol.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Not spotted at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Wilson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, wasn't seen at Thursday's practice, , Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: Wilson also logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday, so the wideout's apparent absence from Wednesday's session sets the stage for Friday's practice to loom large in terms of his availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. In the event that Wilson isn't cleared to play, added targets would be available for some combo of WRs Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams, as well as tight ends Mason Taylor (back) and Kenyon Sadiq.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) absent from Jets practice Thursday
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) is absent from his second straight practice on Thursday as he deals with the concussion that landed him on Wednesday's injury report. Wilson sustained a head injury in a Week 8 loss to the Raiders and has since landed in the NFL's concussion protocol. Should he miss Sunday's Week 9 matchup with the Chiefs, fantasy managers can look to both Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. to see expanded roles, each having featured in recent spike weeks. Mitchell caught seven passes for 142 yards and a score in his first game back from a multi-week absence, while it was Cooper who went for 115 yards and a touchdown in a Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson (concussion) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson (concussion) did not take part in New York's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson was recently placed in the NFL's concussion protocols and wasn't able to practice on Wednesday as a result. It looks like a long shot that he will be cleared to play in time for Sunday's game, and if he's ruled out, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. should both see a substantial increase in opportunities in his absence.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson placed in concussion protocol
metadata.description: The Jets placed WR Garrett Wilson in concussion protocol.
metadata.analysis: Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders. His status for this week is all of a sudden up in the air. If he is ruled out, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. could both step into bigger roles.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - In the NFL's concussion protocol
metadata.description: Wilson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, is considered day-to-day,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: As a result, Wilson's status for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs will need to be tracked closely in the coming days. The wideout is coming off a six-catch, 83-yard effort in the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders, and if Wilson ends up sidelined this weekend, added opportunities would be available for Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson in Concussion Protocol, Considered Day-to-Day
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) is in the league's concussion protocol this week and is considered day-to-day, according to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic. Fantasy managers will now need to keep a close eye on Wilson's practice status this week as the Jets prepare to face the Kansas City Chiefs on the road this Sunday. If the 26-year-old is limited or out this weekend, both Adonai Mitchell and rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. could be must-starts in fantasy football lineups. Wilson caught six of his 12 targets for 83 yards in the Week 8 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, with his 12 targets being the second-highest total of the season. Meanwhile, Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for a career-high 142 yards and a touchdown in his second game back from a finger injury that landed him on Injured Reserve. Wilson has 43 receptions for 527 yards and three touchdowns in eight games so far in 2026 and will be a must-start in fantasy if he can clear the protocol and get the green light to play in a tough road matchup in Week 9.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Not Expected to Be Traded
metadata.description: As the NFL trade deadline approaches and rumors abound about the future of New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson, NFL insider Adam Schefter has shut down any speculation of a trade. "I was told last week, no way they trade him," he said on Tuesday. Speaking specifically about a reunion with quarterback Aaron Rodgers with the Pittsburgh Steelers, he noted, "I don't think people know that full relationship there. I don't know that that would work. That's not happening. Garrett Wilson's not being traded to Pittsburgh." Wilson leads the Jets with 43 receptions for 527 yards and three touchdowns, but he has been outshined in recent weeks by Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson hauls in six passes in Week 8
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-12 targets for 83 yards in a 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Wilson led the team in targets and was second on the team in receptions and receiving yards. This marked his second highest target total of the season, which he needed after being targeted just three times last week. Wilson and the Jets will travel to Kansas City in Week 9.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Targeted 12 times in Week 8 loss
metadata.description: Wilson caught six of 12 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Wilson saw his second-highest target total of the season Sunday after being targeted a season-low three times in the Week 7 loss to Miami. After being outplayed by Omar Cooper in each of the previous two games, Wilson took a back seat to Adonai Mitchell in this one, as Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown while Cooper went without a target. The Jets have three capable wide receivers for the first time in a while, but Wilson easily leads the team with 527 receiving yards heading into a Week 9 road game against the Chiefs, while Mitchell's a distant second with 265 receiving yards.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson not expected to be traded
metadata.description: The Jets are currently not expected to trade WR Garrett Wilson.
metadata.analysis: Wilson told reporters this week that he hasn't requested a trade. It appears the Jets will continue to build around him.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson's Recent Target Share Adds Risk to WR2 Outlook
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson is a WR2 for Sunday's Week 8 home matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, but the recent distribution of targets lowers confidence in a rebound. Wilson received only three of Geno Smith's 30 attempts against Miami, catching two passes for 26 yards while Smith threw three touchdowns. Across Weeks 6-7, Wilson accounted for 12.2% of New York's first-read targets, compared with 29.3% for Omar Cooper Jr. That shift matters because Wilson's disappointing output has come as the offense has gained another productive receiver, rather than simply struggling to move the ball. Wilson still leads the Jets with 37 catches for 444 yards and three touchdowns, and RotoBaller ranks him WR19 for Week 8. Las Vegas allowed Puka Nacua eight catches for 68 yards and a score last week, providing a favorable opportunity if New York directs more passes Wilson's way. Cooper's emergence makes Wilson less appealing as a ceiling play, but his season-long production and the matchup still justify starting him in 12-team leagues.

metadata.title: "No Way" the Jets Trade Garrett Wilson at Deadline
metadata.description: The New York Jets have reportedly "no chance" of trading star wide receiver Garrett Wilson at this year's deadline, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. While the Jets would likely draw significant interest in Wilson, the team has made it clear they have no intention of trading their lead wideout. Wilson showed frustration on the sideline during their 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins after catching just two of three targets for 26 yards. In seven games this season, Wilson has hauled in 37 of 51 passes for 444 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 11.6 half-PPR fantasy points per game. With Wilson likely to remain with the Jets through the 2026 season, his fantasy value will be capped by the limited ceiling of quarterback Geno Smith and a crowded receiving room, as rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. emerges. Fantasy managers should continue to view the fifth-year receiver as a solid WR2 in fantasy and a must-start every week.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Denies trade request talk
metadata.description: Wilson said Wednesday that he won't ask to be traded from the Jets, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Trade talks are heating up across the league and teams in the Jets' position are being looked at as potential sellers at the deadline. Wilson, who has been a Jet since 2022, will not seek a trade from the club, however. The fifth-year wideout is off to a strong start this season, drawing a 25.8 percent target share and averaging 1.98 yards per route run.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Says Trade Request Isn't in His Plans
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson caught two passes for 26 yards on just three targets in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins, and he has drawn only nine targets over his past two games. That has fueled frustration with his involvement in New York's offense, although offensive coordinator Frank Reich acknowledged in Week 7 that the Jets need to involve him earlier. Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic previously reported that New York has no intention of trading Wilson, who signed a four-year, $130 million extension in 2025 that keeps him under contract through 2030. Wilson said Wednesday, according to Rosenblatt, that he will not request a trade despite ongoing speculation about his future, acknowledging he has seen the rumors circulating on social media but is focused on controlling what he can control.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson quiet in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in a 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Wilson turned in his worst performance of the season Sunday, with the star receiver not seeing a target until the second half. Wilson will look to bounce back against Las Vegas in Week 8.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Season-worst performance in Week 7
metadata.description: Wilson caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Wilson wasn't targeted in the first half as the Jets took a 21-7 deficit into the locker room. He was slightly more involved in the second half, but Wilson was overshadowed for a second consecutive game by rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper, who has exceeded 100 receiving yards with a touchdown in both games since recovering from an ankle injury. Wilson will try to bounce back from this season-worst performance in catches, receiving yards and targets when the Jets host the Raiders in Week 8.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Posts Season Lows in Week 7 Loss to Dolphins
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson recorded just two receptions for 26 yards in a 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins in Week 7. It's the second week in a row Wilson recorded under 50 receiving yards, with quarterback Geno Smith favoring wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Mason Taylor in Sunday's home loss. Wilson's target share was expected to decrease since teammate Adonai Mitchell was returning to the lineup, but his season lows badly dent his status as a WR2 in fantasy leagues. Wilson could rebound in Week 8 against a struggling Las Vegas Raiders defense, but he is a bust for Week 7 after recording so little production.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Retains WR2 Appeal as Jets Get Healthier
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson remains a strong WR2 in PPR leagues for Sunday's home matchup against the Miami Dolphins. He has caught 35 of 48 targets for 418 yards and three touchdowns through six games, and his four catches for 44 yards against the New England Patriots in Week 6 were a blip after 100-yard performances against the Detroit Lions and Cleveland Browns over the past four weeks. Both of Wilson's 100-yard games included a touchdown, accounting for two of the Jets' seven passing scores. Target competition is the risk, with Adonai Mitchell's return and Omar Cooper Jr.'s 103-yard outing giving Geno Smith more options.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson is an Inconsistent Option Lately
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson hasn't been a great fantasy option over the last few weeks. Wilson has put together some strong performances, but he has mixed in some duds as well. In Week 4, Wilson finished with three receptions for 27 yards. He followed that up with seven catches for 107 yards and a touchdown in Week 5. This past weekend, Wilson went back to producing duds with four catches for 44 yards in the loss to the New England Patriots. Fantasy managers can't be exactly sure what they're going to get from Wilson right now. Despite some struggles, Wilson is still someone who is viewed as a top option against the Miami Dolphins this weekend.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Four catches in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Wilson brought in four of six targets for 44 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson had an early catch and then had a quiet middle portion of the game before rounding out his line some in the fourth quarter. Wilson still finished with a disappointing line overall, as his reception and receiving yards totals were both his second lowest of the campaign. Geno Smith has undergone his fair share of struggles in his return to New York this season, but Wilson remains his top target with 48 looks from the veteran signal-caller over the first six games. Wilson will take a 35-418-3 line into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson hauls in four passes in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught 4-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Wilson turned in his second lowest output of the season in the loss Sunday. Despite the performance Sunday, Wilson remains the top fantasy option heading into a Week 7 matchup with Miami.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Held in Check While Rookie Teammate Thrives
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson caught four of his six targets for 44 yards during Sunday's Week 6 loss against the New England Patriots. This was just the second time this season that Wilson finished with fewer than 13.0 fantasy points in PPR leagues. His quiet game wasn't necessarily reflective of the Jets' offensive performance as a whole. Instead, he simply wasn't the most productive Jets receiver on Sunday. Wilson ended up being out-produced by rookie Omar Cooper Jr., who caught six passes for 103 yards and one touchdown. There's no question that Wilson is still the top receiver on the depth chart, and he should have no trouble bouncing back as a low-end WR1 against a struggling Miami Dolphins squad in Week 7.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Remains the Jets' Most Reliable Fantasy Option
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson continues to command an overwhelming share of the passing game, an encouraging development with several other offensive players dealing with injuries. Wilson caught seven passes for 104 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against Cleveland in Week 5, giving him his second 100-yard receiving performance of the season. He has now accumulated 31 receptions for 374 yards and three touchdowns on 42 targets through five contests. His involvement should remain substantial against New England, particularly with Adonai Mitchell (finger) officially ruled out. The Patriots will have Christian Gonzalez available again, creating a more challenging individual matchup, although their secondary will be missing Carlton Davis III and Karon Prunty. Wilson's weekly target volume provides a dependable foundation even when New York struggles to sustain drives. He remains a strong WR2 in PPR formats and should be started in most fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson finds the end zone in Week 5
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught seven of his 11 targets for 104 yards and one touchdown in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Wilson easily paced the Jets in receiving, hauling in 104 of the team's 182 passing yards in the close win. He found the end zone on a 32-yard strike from Geno Smith in the first quarter. Wilson has now caught 31 passes for 374 yards and three touchdowns across five games. He will be on the WR1/WR2 borderline in Week 6 against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson's Huge Touchdown Catch Fuels 100-Yard Showing
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson caught seven of his 11 targets for 104 receiving yards and one touchdown during Sunday's Week 5 win over the Cleveland Browns. After a disappointing outing in Week 4, Wilson got back on track this weekend with his second-best fantasy performance of the season. The 26-year-old has solidified himself as a WR1 in fantasy football, and he has fared better with Geno Smith at quarterback than he did with a combination of Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor, and Brady Cook in 2025. Although we can't guarantee that Smith will be able to support top-tier production from Wilson every week, the duo has certainly looked solid so far. Wilson is a potential WR1 option for Week 6 against New England, but his exact outlook will depend on whether Patriots cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Carlton Davis III (neck) play next Sunday.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Bounces back with 104 yards, TD
metadata.description: Wilson caught seven of 11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Wilson opened the scoring with a 32-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter. That was his third touchdown grab through five games, and Wilson has exceeded 100 receiving yards twice while working as the top receiver for the Jets. No teammate topped 26 receiving yards as wide receivers Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper (ankle), as well as running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) were inactive, while tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) exited in the second half. Up next for Wilson and the 2-3 Jets is a trip to New England to face the Patriots in Week 6.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Remains a Strong WR2 Despite Recent Struggles
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson managed just three catches for 27 yards against Chicago, although the entire offense struggled in a game where Geno Smith attempted only 15 passes. Wilson still accounts for a significant portion of New York's passing game, with 24 receptions for 270 yards and two touchdowns through four weeks. The Jets will be without Adonai Mitchell again Sunday, and that should keep Wilson heavily involved against Cleveland. The matchup isn't ideal, particularly with the Browns recording at least three sacks in three straight games, but Wilson's target share gives him a much better outlook than the team's recent offensive performances might suggest. RotoBaller has him at WR15 for Week 5. The Jets need to give Smith more opportunities to throw if Wilson is going to produce, but he's still their best fantasy option in the passing game.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson held to 27 yards in Week 4
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught three of his four targets for 27 yards in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Wilson and the Jets struggled to get anything going in the loss to Chicago. The Jets were held to just 119 passing yards, with most of the damage coming via a 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams. Wilson has caught 24 passes for 270 yards and two touchdowns through four games. He will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in fantasy in a Week 5 home matchup against the Browns.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Struggles along with entire offense Week 4
metadata.description: Wilson caught three of four targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Wilson accounted for two of Geno Smith's three completions in the first half, and the star wide receiver finished with a team-high three catches as Smith completed only eight passes in a forgettable performance from New York's offense. Heading into Sunday's loss, Wilson had been averaging seven catches for 81 receiving yards per game. Wilson and the Jets will try to bounce back from this dud in Week 5 against the Browns.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson is Quiet in Week 4 Loss
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson was unable to carry his momentum from Week 3 into this weekend's matchup against the Chicago Bears. Wilson was quiet with three receptions on four targets for 27 yards in the loss. It wasn't all his fault, as the Jets only possessed the ball for 17 minutes in this game. His four targets actually led the team, with quarterback Geno Smith only attempting 15 total passes. Fantasy managers should expect better days ahead for Wilson with a matchup against the Cleveland Browns in Week 5. Wilson should bounce back into WR1 territory for that one.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Remains a Must-Start WR1
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson is coming off 10 catches for 107 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets, and the Jets may need him even more in Chicago. Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell, and Mason Taylor have all been ruled out, leaving fewer proven options around Geno Smith. Wilson already has 27 targets through three games, with 21 catches for 243 yards and two scores, so volume wasn't exactly a problem before the injuries piled up. Chicago's defense looked much better Monday night against Philadelphia, but that isn't enough to move Wilson out of the lineup. He's WR5 in RotoBaller's Week 4 rankings and remains the clear centerpiece of the Jets passing game. Treat him as a WR1 and move on.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson hauls in 10 passes in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught 10-of-13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Lions.
metadata.analysis: Wilson caught a 24-yard strike from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter to tie the game. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Wilson's status early in the week as he did exit with an injury on the final drive. Wilson and the Jets will take on the Bears in Week 4.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Big day in loss to Lions
metadata.description: Wilson caught 10 of 13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to Detroit.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout paced Jets pass catchers in all three receiving categories, and his 23-yard TD from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter tied the game at 24-24, only for the Lions to respond inside the final two minutes. It's Wilson's first 100-yard performance since Week 14 of the 2024 season, as injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign. Wilson has also found the end zone in back-to-back games, and he'll take a 21-243-2 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson exits Sunday
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson exited Sunday's contest between the New York Jets and Detroit Lions with an apparent injury.
metadata.analysis: Wilson was seen limping to the sideline late in the fourth quarter for head coach Aaron Glenn, hauling in 10 of his team-leading 13 targets for 107 yards and one touchdown before exiting.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Clears Concussion Evaluation
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (head) suffered a head injury on the team's final possession of its loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 3. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Wilson cleared his head evaluation, so "he should be just fine". Wilson cleared the protocol on the sidelines but did not have time to get back into the game. Wilson had 10 catches for 107 receiving yards and a touchdown prior to exiting on the final drive of the game.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Posts 100-Plus Yards, Draws Injury Concerns in Week 3
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson caught 10 receptions for 107 yards and one touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 road loss to the Detroit Lions, and gave fantasy managers a scare toward the end of the game. The veteran wideout took a hard hit while diving for a catch from Geno Smith and spent a brief stint in the medical tent. Wilson was Smith's top target on Sunday, with Adonai Mitchell (finger) ruled out before kickoff. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on Wilson's status through the next week.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Draws One of His Better Matchups
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson caught five of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown against Green Bay, giving him 11 catches for 136 yards through two games. Adonai Mitchell drew more targets last week, but Wilson remains Geno Smith's top established option and has caught Smith's only passing touchdown of the season. Detroit has already given up six passing touchdowns through two games. Tyler Shough threw for 410 yards and three scores against the Lions in Week 1, and Josh Allen added another three touchdowns last Thursday. RotoBaller ranks Wilson as the WR12 for Week 3. Mitchell's growing role gives New York another legitimate option on the other side, but Wilson remains an easy fantasy start and carries WR1 upside in this matchup.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Remains an Impactful Piece
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson is finally showing how impactful he can be on the field after an injury-riddled 2025 campaign. Through two games, Wilson has hauled in 11 receptions for 136 yards and one touchdown. The 26-year-old has accounted for the lone touchdown that quarterback Geno Smith has thrown this season. Adonai Mitchell saw 12 targets last week, but Wilson remains the much better fantasy option between the two. Wilson has big-play ability that looks tempting ahead of a juicy matchup against the Detroit Lions defense in Week 3. The Jets are without rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) right now, so Wilson and Mitchell will be leaned on in the receiving game.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson finds end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson hauled in five of his seven targets for 57 yards and one touchdown in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
metadata.analysis: Wilson continues to make the most of sizeable involvement in an underperforming passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful options as part of a Jets offense filled with more questions than answers early on ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Scores in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Wilson caught five of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Wilson broke a 7-7 tie with a five-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, but the Jets ultimately failed to close the game out after taking a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter. Adonai Mitchell led the Jets with 12 targets and tied Breece Hall for the team receiving yards lead at 63. Wilson figures to operate as the team's top pass catcher most weeks, as he did in the season-opening win over the Titans, and the 2022 first-round pick has accounted for Geno Smith's lone touchdown pass through two games. Up next for Wilson and the Jets is a juicy Week 3 matchup against the struggling Lions secondary.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Remains the Clear No. 1 Target
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson did not score in Week 1, but there was no question about where quarterback Geno Smith looked first. Wilson caught six of seven targets for 79 yards, including a 31-yard grab, and no other Jets player saw more than three targets. Omar Cooper Jr. is also out this week with an ankle injury, which does nothing to hurt Wilson's grip on the passing game. Green Bay gave up eight catches, 92 yards, and two touchdowns to Justin Jefferson in the opener, even though Minnesota did not pile up much passing yardage overall. Wilson sits at WR12 in RotoBaller's Week 2 rankings. The Jets may still prefer to run when they can, but Wilson's share is big enough that he does not need a huge passing day from Smith to return solid fantasy value.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Eyeing Larger Target Share With Rookie WR Injured
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson has always had plenty of talent after the Jets took him 10th overall in the 2022 NFL Draft from Ohio State, but the problem is he has never worked with a good enough quarterback in the Big Apple to help him reach his true potential. Fantasy managers mostly overlooked the 26-year-old going into his fifth year in the league because he is working with veteran quarterback Geno Smith, who was disastrous in 2025 with the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson had a solid showing in the Week 1 season-opening win over the Tennessee Titans, catching six of his seven targets for 79 yards, although he did not find the end zone. He was already New York's unquestioned WR1, but the expected multi-week injury to rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is going to open up even more targets for Wilson as the Jets head into their Week 2 matchup at home against the Green Bay Packers this Sunday. Wilson is not in a sexy situation with Gang Green, but he will have WR1 upside in fantasy with Cooper sidelined.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson goes for 79 yards in Week 1
metadata.description: Garrett Wilson caught six of his seven targets for 79 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Wilson led the Jets in all receiving categories in the easy win over an overmatched Tennessee team. Even though it wasn't a huge performance from Wilson, it was an encouraging debut for the receiver with Geno Smith at the helm. Wilson settles in as a high-end WR2 in a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Leading receiver in Week 1 win
metadata.description: Wilson caught six of seven targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: Wilson paced the team in targets, catches and receiving yards while no teammate exceeded three targets as the Jets employed a run-heavy approach while playing from ahead. Poor QB play and a knee injury limited Wilson to a career-low 395 receiving yards in seven appearances last season, but he had at least 1,042 receiving yards in each of his first three campaigns. Wilson is set to continue working as the top target for offseason acquisition Geno Smith in Week 2 against the Packers.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson Brings WR1 Upside Into Season Opener
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson returns healthy for Sunday's opener against Tennessee after a knee injury limited him to seven games in 2025. Wilson still caught 36 passes for 395 yards and four touchdowns during the shortened season, and his last full campaign showed the volume he can command. He finished 2024 with 101 receptions for 1,104 yards and seven touchdowns, completing a run of three straight 1,000-yard seasons to begin his career. Geno Smith now takes over at quarterback, with Wilson remaining the clear No. 1 option in Frank Reich's offense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing touchdowns and 8.2 yards per attempt last season, although Robert Saleh has since taken over as head coach. RotoBaller ranks Wilson WR15 for Week 1. His target ceiling makes him a strong high-end WR2 with a realistic path to WR1 production in the opener.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson - Top target in revamped Jets offense
metadata.description: Wilson is set to top a Jets wide receiver depth chart that also includes Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper, Isaiah Williams, Tim Patrick and Arian Smith, Randy Lange of the Jets' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Wilson led the Jets with 395 receiving yards in 2025 despite missing 10 of the last 11 games due to a knee injury. The 2022 first-round pick has regained health, while the passing offense around him has undergone a significant makeover, with veteran QB Geno Smith and rookie first-round pass catchers Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq (abdomen) among the team's most notable additions. Wilson exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first three NFL seasons despite uneven QB play prior to falling well short of that mark in his injury-shortened fourth campaign.

metadata.title: Garrett Wilson's Stock Rebounds After Healthy Summer
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson looks a lot easier to buy into after making it through the summer without any issues from the knee injury that derailed his 2025 season. Wilson played only seven games last year, finishing with 36 catches for 395 yards and four touchdowns on 59 targets after opening his career with three straight 1,000-yard seasons. This summer has looked much more normal. He practiced throughout camp, aside from one illness-related absence, and caught three passes for 42 yards across two preseason appearances. The connection with new quarterback Geno Smith showed up repeatedly in practice, including a five-for-five stretch when Smith targeted Wilson during team work on Aug. 7. Wilson is still the clear No. 1 receiver on New York's depth chart, even with Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr. and a deeper group of pass catchers around him. RotoBaller has him at WR18 in its latest half-PPR rankings. After last year's lost season, a healthy Wilson looks like a solid WR2 with room to climb back toward the WR1 conversation.
